name: Fund, direct and co-investment
objective: Explain and apply fund, direct and co-investment.
explanation: Fund investing delegates selection to a manager and often adds fees. Direct investing gives control but requires expertise and capital. Co-investment provides participation alongside a fund, with its own due-diligence demands.
why: The separate alongside investment is a co-investment and can increase concentration.
definition: Fund investing delegates selection to a manager and often adds fees.
example: An investor buys a stake in one private company alongside its fund manager: a co-investment rather than another diversified fund commitment.
trap: Lower fees do not eliminate concentration or execution risk.
mnemonic: Fund, direct and co-investment → Lower fees do not eliminate concentration or execution risk.
recall: Without looking: explain fund, direct and co-investment and one mistake to avoid.
recallAnswer: Fund investing delegates selection to a manager and often adds fees. Direct investing gives control but requires expertise and capital. Co-investment provides participation alongside a fund, with its own due-diligence demands. Watch for: Lower fees do not eliminate concentration or execution risk.
